letters-to-his-children: Theodore Roosevelt the Rough Rider and president was also a devoted, playful father, as these letters prove. He writes to his children about bear hunts and birds' nests, White House pets and family jokes, in a warm, boyish voice. The collection shows the human side of a larger-than-life figure — tender, funny, and endlessly curious.
advice-to-a-mother-on-the-management-of-: Victorian physician Pye Henry Chavasse wrote this famous manual to guide mothers through feeding, illness, and the daily care of infants and children. Immensely popular in its day, it was the Dr. Spock of the 1800s — though its advice now reads as a fascinating mix of wisdom and period error. A revealing look at how our great-grandmothers raised babies.
canada-for-gentlemen: James Seton Cockburn writes for the British sportsman and settler with an eye on Canada — its hunting, fishing, farms, and wide-open chances. Sound tips mix with warm praise of the young Dominion's promise. A lively guidebook from the days when Canada was calling young Englishmen west.
bonnie-prince-charlie-a-tale-of-fontenoy: G. A. Henty's Jacobite adventure follows a young hero through Fontenoy and Culloden alongside Bonnie Prince Charlie. Battles, narrow escapes, and Highland loyalty fill this stirring tale of the Forty-Five. History's romance at full Henty throttle, written for boys who loved a hero.
the-angel-adjutant-of-twice-born-men: Minnie Carpenter, a Salvation Army officer, recalls Kate Lee — the Angel Adjutant — whose work among the poor of London won countless souls. A tribute to a saint of the slums. Warm, earnest, and deeply moving. Her tireless love for London's poorest won her the name of angel, and countless grateful hearts.
marching-men: Sherwood Anderson's early novel follows Beaut McGregor, a young laborer who dreams of leading marching men to a new order. The author's brooding power is already at work. A strange, strong book from the writer of Winesburg, Ohio. His dream of disciplined workers marching toward a new day haunts this strange, powerful early novel.
kathleen: Christopher Morley, the beloved essayist, tells of Kathleen in this gentle novel — a story of youth, books, and the charm of everyday life. His warm, bookish humor glows throughout. A delightful minor work from a major charmer. College days, first love, and literary talk fill this warm, gentle story of youth.
celtic-tales-told-to-the-children: Louey Chisholm retells Celtic tales for children — Cuchulain, Fionn, Deirdre, and the old heroes of Ireland and Scotland. Her clear, lively versions open the Celtic world to young readers. Enchanting stories, beautifully and simply told. Giants, fairies, and heroes step gaily through her pages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aachen: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia piece on Aachen — Charlemagne's city of the great cathedral — covers its past, its shrine, and its kings. Joseph Lins keeps the facts straight and the story clear. A handy, solid reference on a famous old German town.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: This article treats Saint-Ouen of Rouen, famed for its soaring Gothic church. The monks' pride still lifts Norman eyes. Gilbert Huddleston recounts its past. A crown of stone over Rouen. Its great organ is famed throughout Normandy. Its tower crowns the Rouen skyline.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-wald: The Encyclopedia's Waldsassen entry: the Bavarian Cistercian house of the famous library. Wood and gold frame its book hall. Edmond Obrecht gives its history. A jewel of the Oberpfalz. Its basilica glitters with southern German Baroque. Its nuns keep the old Cistercian rule.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aberdeen: This 1913 reference article on Aberdeen — the Scottish diocese, old and new. John Joseph A'Becket traces its bishops through penal days. The granite city's Catholic story, told with care. Scotland's north-east in church history. Its bishop hid priests in the penal times.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-contzen: This 1913 reference article on Adam Contzen — the Jesuit confessor of Maximilian of Bavaria. Benedict Guldner sketches his influence. He steered a prince through the Thirty Years' War. A confessor behind the throne.
